Subject: Billing stack RFP — quick scheduling and MSA requests

Hi BrightBill / Ramp reps,

Thanks for the fast responses to our RFP so far. High-level context: Redwood is evaluating a replacement/upgrade for our billing and expense stack ahead of a subscription model change in Q1. We're trying to land a pilot vendor by end of November so procurement can lock commercial terms in December.

Two asks to move forward:
1) Can BrightBill share a redline-able MSA and confirmation on data residency (US only)?
2) Ramp — please confirm whether your expense product supports billable project codes and custom export formats for our accounting team.

I've attached the RFP workbook (RFP_BillingStack_2025.xlsx) for reference.

Proposed next steps:
- BrightBill: MSA + sample integration checklist by Friday 11/07
- NetSuite: we'll keep the pricing for reference (cc'd) but immediate priority is vendor that can support billing run automation and our usage-based metering.

Thanks —
Laura Bennett
Head of Finance Ops
Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
[attachment: RFP_BillingStack_2025.xlsx (xlsx)]
From: markus.klein@redwood.com
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, michael.grant@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 06 Nov 2025 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Billing stack RFP — internal note

Laura / Michael — quick internal read:
- NetSuite is expected; good for long-term accounting integrations but higher TCO and longer lead time.
- BrightBill looks promising for billing orchestration and usage-based pricing; faster time-to-value.
- Ramp is strong for expense and card workflow, but Ramp's export formats sometimes need a light ETL layer for our GL mapping.

If we prioritize a December contract slot and a Jan pilot, I'd push BrightBill for billing + NetSuite for accounting synchronization post-pilot. We can use Ramp for employee expenses in a separate procurement if the timeline doesn't align.

-MK

Team — thanks for the quick turnaround this week. Summary and proposed decisions so we can close the procurement window: 

1) Pilot selection: BrightBill — pilot MSA received with US-only residency and pilot waiver. I recommend we accept pilot terms and run a 3-month pilot starting Jan 6.
2) NetSuite: keep pricing packet on file. Plan for post-pilot sync (integration cost estimate in Netsuite_pricing_v2.pdf).
3) Expense tool: proceed with Ramp for T&E (no blocking concerns), procurement to run a separate PO in early Dec.

Open asks before I sign the pilot MSA: 
- Michael: confirm budget commit of $0 for pilot (waived setup) and up to $50k reserved contingency for integration work.
- Stephanie: confirm security questionnaire answers and indicate if any additional evidence needed (SOC2, penetration test report).
- Markus: expedite 2-hour integration scoping session with BrightBill technical lead next week.

If I don't hear objections by EOD Thursday 11/13 I'll instruct BrightBill to send the DocuSign for signature.

Thanks —
Laura Bennett
Head of Finance Ops, Redwood Inference
